nodes.title: Frames and u-morphisms of frames
nodes.statement: A frame is (A, Fil A, φ, φ₁, ϖ): A is a commutative ring, Fil A an ideal, φ a Frobenius lift modulo p, φ₁ : Fil A → A a φ-semilinear additive map, and ϖ ∈ A with φ(b) = ϖφ₁(b) for b ∈ Fil A. Require Fil A + pA ⊆ Rad(A); write R = A/Fil A. A u-morphism α to a second frame, for u ∈ A′×, is a ring map commuting with Frobenius, preserving Fil, and satisfying φ′₁α = uαφ₁ and α(ϖ) = uϖ′.
hypotheses: p is prime. This is Cais–Lau Definition 2.1.1, with ϖ bundled. No topology is part of a general frame. Completeness, henselianity and continuity are imposed in the individual results that use them.
If φ₁(Fil A) generates the unit ideal then ϖ is determined by φ and φ₁. Lau 2010 imposes that generation condition; it is not imposed in the general convention here.
Anschütz–Le Bras Definition 4.1.16 uses a more specific completeness convention. The prismatic applications below satisfy the radical condition.
proofSteps: Bundle the ring, ideal, semilinear map and scalar with their equations; use Cais–Lau Definition 2.1.1 for the radical condition. A quotient ring and the category of such structures use the existing ring/ideal carriers.
u-morphisms compose: a u-morphism followed by a u′-morphism is a (α′(u)·u′)-morphism; identities are 1-morphisms.
acceptance: For an oriented prism (A, (d)) the two structures of node prism-frames are frames, with ϖ = φ(d) and ϖ = d respectively.
The Witt frame of a p-adically complete ring (node PD.7/witt-frame) is a frame with ϖ = p.

nodes.title: The d-frame and the Nygaard frame of an oriented prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I = (d)) be an oriented bounded prism (A is d-torsion-free). (1) The d-frame A_d = (A, (d), φ, φ₁, φ(d)) has φ₁(dx) = φ(x) for x ∈ A. (2) If d = φ(d′) for some d′ ∈ A, the Nygaard frame A_Nyg = (A, N^{≥1}A, φ, φ₁, d) has Fil = N^{≥1}A = φ^{-1}(dA) and φ₁ = φ/d on N^{≥1}A. In (1) the divided Frobenius is with respect to φ(d); in (2) with respect to d.
hypotheses: (A, (d)) is an oriented bounded prism: a prism with a chosen generator d of I (PrismaticCohomology PR.0). For (2), d lies in the image of φ; this holds for perfect prisms and for the prisms of quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings over a perfect prism.
N^{≥1}A = φ^{-1}(IA) is the first Nygaard piece of the prism.
proofSteps: d-torsion-freeness of A makes φ₁ in (1) well defined; φ(dx) = φ(d)φ(x) gives φ = φ(d)φ₁ on (d).
For (2), N^{≥1}A = φ^{-1}(dA) and d-torsion-freeness define φ/d; φ₁ is φ-semilinear since φ(ab) = φ(a)φ(b).

For a bounded prism A is classically (p,d)-complete, so (p,d) ⊆ Rad(A). If x ∈ N≥1A, then x^p ∈ (p,d), so N≥1A ⊆ Rad(A) too. This verifies both frame radical conditions. No assertion about completeness of an arbitrary quotient is needed (AL23 Example 4.1.18, p. 32).
acceptance: For the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)⟦u⟧, (E(u))) the d-frame is the frame of Breuil windows of Lau 2010.
For a perfect prism (A_inf(S), (ξ̃)) with ξ̃ = φ(ξ), the Nygaard frame has N^{≥1}A = (ξ), and it coincides with the d-frame for d = ξ.

nodes.title: Windows over a frame
nodes.statement: A window over a frame 𝒜 = (A, Fil A, φ, φ₁, ϖ) is a quadruple M = (M, Fil M, φ_M, φ_{M,1}) with M a finite projective A-module, Fil M ⊆ M an A-submodule and φ-semilinear maps φ_M : M → M, φ_{M,1} : Fil M → M such that (i) Fil A·M ⊆ Fil M and M/Fil M is a finite projective R-module, R = A/Fil A; (ii) φ_{M,1}(am) = φ₁(a)φ_M(m) for a ∈ Fil A, m ∈ M; (iii) φ_M(m) = ϖ·φ_{M,1}(m) for m ∈ Fil M; (iv) φ_{M,1}(Fil M) + φ_M(M) generates M as an A-module. Morphisms are A-linear maps preserving the filtrations and commuting with φ_M and φ_{M,1}; the category is Win(𝒜).
hypotheses: When the image of φ₁ generates the unit ideal, (iii) follows from (ii) and (iv) says that φ_{M,1}(Fil M) generates M (Anschütz–Le Bras, Remark 4.1.20).
proofSteps: Bundle the data and the four axioms; morphisms form an additive category with finite direct sums computed componentwise (Anschütz–Le Bras, Definition 4.1.19, p. 32).
acceptance: The unit window (A, Fil A, φ, φ₁) works over every frame in the chosen convention: φ(1) = 1 already gives generation.

nodes.title: α-morphisms of windows and base change along u-morphisms of frames
nodes.statement: Let α : 𝒜 → 𝒜′ be a u-morphism of frames. An α-morphism of windows f : M → M′ (M ∈ Win(𝒜), M′ ∈ Win(𝒜′)) is an α-linear map with f ∘ φ_M = φ_{M′} ∘ f, f(Fil M) ⊆ Fil M′ and φ_{M′,1} ∘ f = u·(f ∘ φ_{M,1}). There is a functor α^* : Win(𝒜) → Win(𝒜′) with Hom_{Win(𝒜′)}(α^*M, M′) = {α-morphisms M → M′}; concretely α^*M = A′ ⊗_A M, Fil(α^*M) is generated by Fil A′·α^*M and the image of Fil M, and φ, φ₁ on α^*M are the unique maps making m ↦ 1 ⊗ m an α-morphism.
hypotheses: Frames as in node frame; u ∈ A′^×.

The source windows admit normal decompositions; in particular this holds when (A, Fil A) is henselian, as in the applications here. This avoids deducing projective lifting merely from the radical condition.
proofSteps: Choose a normal decomposition M = L ⊕ T, Fil M = L ⊕ Fil A·T. Extend its two Frobenius maps, multiplying the divided map by u as required. Independence of the decomposition follows from the α-morphism universal property (AL23 Remark 4.1.21, pp. 32–33; Cais–Lau §2.1, pp. 4–5).
The universal property follows from the uniqueness of the extension of semilinear maps along A → A′.
Functoriality: (α′ ∘ α)^* ≅ α′^* ∘ α^* for composable u- and u′-morphisms.
acceptance: For α the identity 1-morphism, α^* is the identity and α-morphisms are window morphisms.
Base change preserves the rank of M and the rank of the Hodge quotient M/Fil M.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules over a henselian pair
nodes.statement: Let (A, J) be a henselian pair. Then M ↦ M/JM induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of finite projective A-modules and of finite projective A/J-modules; moreover every isomorphism M/JM ≅ N/JN of reductions of finite projective A-modules lifts to an isomorphism M ≅ N.
hypotheses: (A, J) henselian in the sense of Mathlib HenselianRing A J (J in the Jacobson radical, and monic polynomials with a simple root modulo J lift it).
proofSteps: Injectivity: lift an isomorphism by projectivity of M; it is surjective by Nakayama since J lies in the Jacobson radical, and an isomorphism because its source and target are projective of equal rank at every point (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.1.27, p. 35).

Surjectivity: every finite projective A/J-module lifts to a finite projective A-module along a henselian pair (Stacks, Tag 0D4A, which reduces to lifting idempotents of finite étale algebras along henselian pairs).
acceptance: For A complete local noetherian and J its maximal ideal, every finite projective module is free, matching the lifting of free modules.
For J locally nilpotent the statement is the classical lifting of projective modules over nilpotent thickenings.

nodes.title: Normal decompositions of windows
nodes.statement: Let 𝒜 = (A, Fil A, φ, φ₁, ϖ) be a frame such that every finite projective A/Fil A-module lifts to a finite projective A-module. (1) Every window M over 𝒜 has a normal decomposition: finite projective A-modules L, T with M = L ⊕ T and Fil M = L ⊕ Fil A·T. (2) Given L and T, window structures on (L ⊕ T, L ⊕ Fil A·T) correspond bijectively to φ-semilinear maps Ψ : L ⊕ T → L ⊕ T whose linearisation is an isomorphism, by Ψ(l + t) = φ_{M,1}(l) + φ_M(t), with inverse φ_M(l + t) = ϖΨ(l) + Ψ(t) and φ_{M,1}(l + at) = Ψ(l) + φ₁(a)Ψ(t) for a ∈ Fil A.
hypotheses: The lifting hypothesis holds when (A, Fil A) is henselian (node henselian-projective-lifting), in particular for the Nygaard frame of Δ_R with R quasi-regular semiperfectoid (node PD.1/qrsp-prism-henselian).
proofSteps: Write S = A/Fil A; S ⊗_A M ≅ M/Fil M ⊕ Q with Q finite projective since M/Fil M is; lift Q to L and M/Fil M to T and lift the decomposition by projectivity; then Fil M = L ⊕ Fil A·T (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.1.22, p. 33, after Lau 2010, Remark 2.4 and Lemma 2.5).

Given the window, Ψ defined by the formula is semilinear and its linearisation is surjective by axiom (iv), hence an isomorphism of finite projective modules of equal rank; conversely the displayed formulas satisfy axioms (ii)–(iv).
acceptance: For the unit window of A_d, L = 0 and T = A, with Ψ = φ.
For a window over a perfect field frame (W(k), p, F, F/p), a normal decomposition is a choice of a complement to the Hodge filtration in the classical Dieudonné module.

nodes.title: The filtration of a window is the Frobenius preimage of ϖM
nodes.statement: Let 𝒜 be a frame as in node normal-decomposition with ϖ a nonzerodivisor of A and Fil A = φ^{-1}(ϖA). For every window M over 𝒜: (1) Fil M = φ_M^{-1}(ϖM); (2) φ_M induces an injection M/Fil M → M/ϖM, which extends to an injection (A/ϖ) ⊗_{A/Fil A} (M/Fil M) → M/ϖM onto a locally direct summand. In particular a morphism of A-modules between windows commuting with φ_M is a morphism of windows.
hypotheses: ϖ is a nonzerodivisor and Fil A = φ^{-1}(ϖA); projectives lift along A → A/Fil A.
proofSteps: Fil M ⊆ φ_M^{-1}(ϖM) by axiom (iii).

Choose a normal decomposition M = L ⊕ T with Ψ; for x = l + t, φ_M(x) = ϖΨ(l) + Ψ(t), so φ_M(x) ∈ ϖM iff Ψ(t) ∈ ϖM. Localise so that L, T are free; Ψ(t₁), …, Ψ(t_r), Ψ(l₁), …, Ψ(l_s) is a basis of M, so Σφ(aᵢ)Ψ(tᵢ) ∈ ϖM forces φ(aᵢ) ∈ ϖA, i.e. aᵢ ∈ Fil A, hence t ∈ Fil A·T (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.1.23, pp. 33–34).
The map M/Fil M ≅ T/Fil A·T → M/ϖM is induced by Ψ on T, whose image is part of a basis modulo ϖ; this gives the injective map onto a direct summand.
The last sentence: Fil M is determined by φ_M, and φ_{M,1} = φ_M/ϖ on it because ϖ is a nonzerodivisor.
acceptance: For the Nygaard frame of Δ_R (R quasi-regular semiperfectoid) the hypotheses hold with ϖ = ξ̃ and Fil = N^{≥1}Δ_R = φ^{-1}(ξ̃Δ_R).
The injectivity in (2) is exactly the admissibility condition of node PD.1/prismatic-dieudonne-module.

nodes.title: Minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules over a prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism. A Breuil–Kisin module over (A, I) is an F-crystal over the single prism (A, I) in the sense of PrismaticCohomology PR.7 (a finite projective A-module M with an isomorphism φ_M : (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I]). It is minuscule if φ_M maps φ^*M into M and the cokernel of φ_M : φ^*M → M is killed by I. BK_min(A) is the full subcategory of minuscule objects; morphisms are A-linear maps commuting with φ_M.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a bounded prism. The definition follows Anschütz–Le Bras, Definition 4.1.24, which asks M finite projective; for local statements finite projective and finite projective agree after localisation on Spec A.
Minuscule means effective in the sense of PR.7 with cokernel killed by I; effective alone (cokernel killed by a power of I) is weaker.

A principal prism ideal does not imply that every finite projective module is free. Freeness is only asserted locally. Naive duality below uses the chosen generator d; an orientation-independent version requires the rank-one twist.

AL23 Definition 4.1.24 is phrased for finite free modules. The finite-projective convention here is its Zariski-local extension, justified by Cais–Lau Definition 2.1.13 and descent of the localized Frobenius map. This is an explicit generalization, not a claim that AL23 calls every projective module free.
proofSteps: Define the predicate on PrismaticCohomology PR.7/f-crystal-over-prism: effectivity plus I·coker(φ_M) = 0.

Closure under finite direct sums and base change along maps of prisms: the image condition and the annihilation by I are preserved because I·B = J for a map (A, I) → (B, J) (PrismaticCohomology PR.0, rigidity).
Duality: M ↦ M^∨ with Frobenius d·(φ_M^∨)^{-1} (d a local generator of I) preserves minuscule objects (after Anschütz–Le Bras, Remark 4.1.11, and AInfCohomology AI.2.4).
acceptance: The unit (A, φ) is minuscule with zero cokernel; its twist (A, d·φ) is minuscule with cokernel A/I.

nodes.title: The cokernel of a minuscule Breuil–Kisin module is finite projective over A/I
nodes.statement: Let (M, φ_M) be a minuscule Breuil–Kisin module over a bounded prism (A, I). Then N = coker(φ_M : φ^*M → M) is a finite projective A/I-module, and φ_M : φ^*M → M is injective.
hypotheses: (A, I) bounded prism; M finite projective.
proofSteps: Injectivity: φ_M becomes an isomorphism after inverting I and φ^*M is I-torsion-free.
N has the two-term resolution 0 → φ^*M → M → N → 0 by finite projective A-modules, so it is pseudocoherent over A, hence over A/I.

At a closed point of Spec(A/I) with residue field k, k̄ ⊗^L_{A/I} N ≅ W(k̄) ⊗^L_A N is a perfect W(k̄)-complex, hence bounded; so N has finite Tor dimension over A/I and a finite resolution by finite projectives (Stacks, Tag 068W). Projective dimension ≤ 1 over A then forces N projective over A/I (Anschütz–Le Bras, Remark 4.1.25, p. 34).

At a closed geometric residue field k̄ of A/I use the canonical δ-map A→W(k̄). The two-term projective resolution gives a bounded derived fibre. Stacks Tag 068W applied to the pseudocoherent A/I-module N gives finite projective dimension. Since pd_A(N)≤1 and I is a Cartier divisor killing N, the local change-of-rings dimension shift gives pd_(A/I)(N)=0. This is the argument of AL23 Remark 4.1.25, p. 34, and uses derived fibres rather than naive fibre dimensions.
acceptance: For (A, d·φ) the cokernel A/I is free of rank one over A/I.

nodes.title: Windows over the d-frame are minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules (Cais–Lau)
nodes.statement: Let (A, (d)) be an oriented bounded prism. The functor (M, Fil M, φ_M, φ_{M,1}) ↦ (Fil M, d·φ_{M,1}) is an equivalence Win(A_d) ≃ BK_min(A), where the Frobenius of the target is the linearisation of d·φ_{M,1}|_{Fil M}.
hypotheses: A is d-torsion-free; the d-frame A_d of node prism-frames.
The pair (A,(d)) is henselian in the bounded-prism setting, so finite projectives over A/d lift, as required by CL17 Lemma 2.1.16.
proofSteps: A d-frame window gives the BT module N=Fil M with semilinear Frobenius d·φ_{M,1} : N→N. The factor d is needed to land in Fil M. Normal decomposition makes N finite projective and its linearized Frobenius cokernel finite projective over A/d and killed by d (AL23 Proposition 4.1.26, p. 34; CL17 Lemma 2.1.16, p. 7).

Conversely write Φ : φ*N → N for the injective Frobenius linearization. There is a unique ψ : N → φ*N with Φψ = d and ψΦ = d. Set M = φ*N and Fil M = ψ(N), which contains dM. Define φ_{M,1}(ψx) = 1⊗x and φ_M(1⊗x) = 1⊗Φ(1⊗x), extended φ-semilinearly. Injectivity of ψ makes the first formula well defined.

Apply the projective-cokernel result also to the dual matrix factorization to show M/ψN is finite projective over A/d. The two constructions satisfy the window equations and undo each other naturally.
acceptance: For the Breuil–Kisin prism over 𝒪_K this is the equivalence between Breuil windows and Kisin modules of E-height ≤ 1 used by Lau 2010.
The unit window of A_d corresponds to (A, d·φ), the minuscule twist.

nodes.title: Unit Frobenius modules deform uniquely along nilpotent surjections
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a surjection of bounded prisms with kernel J such that φ is topologically nilpotent on J for the (p, I)-adic topology and (A, J) is henselian. Then base change (M, φ_M) ↦ (M ⊗_A B, φ_M ⊗ B) is an equivalence from unit φ-modules over A (finite projective M with φ_M : φ^*M ≅ M) to unit φ-modules over B.
hypotheses: φ topologically nilpotent on J: φ^j(a) → 0 for every a ∈ J.
proofSteps: Full faithfulness reduces, via internal Hom, to M^{φ_M = 1} ≅ (M/JM)^{φ_M = 1}: injectivity since a fixed m ∈ JM equals φ_M^j(m) → 0; surjectivity by the convergent correction m + Σ_j φ_M^j(φ_M(m) − m).

Essential surjectivity: lift the module by node henselian-projective-lifting and the linearised Frobenius by projectivity; it is an isomorphism because J lies in the Jacobson radical (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.1.31, pp. 36–37).
acceptance: For B = A/J with J = 0 the statement is trivial.
For A = W(k)⟦u⟧ → W(k) (u ↦ 0) with φ(u) = u^p, φ is topologically nilpotent on (u), and unit φ-modules over the Breuil–Kisin prism are base changed from W(k).

nodes.title: Windows deform along surjections with topologically nilpotent divided Frobenius
nodes.statement: (1) Let (A, (ξ̃)) → (B, (ξ̃)) be a surjection of oriented bounded prisms with ξ̃ = φ(ξ), kernel J ⊆ N^{≥1}A, (A, J) henselian and φ₁ = φ/ξ̃ pointwise topologically nilpotent on J. Then φ₁(J) ⊆ J, ℬ = (B, N^{≥1}A/J, φ, φ₁, ξ̃) is a frame, and base change Win(A_Nyg) → Win(ℬ) is an equivalence. (2) More generally, if α : 𝒜 → 𝒜′ is a 1-morphism of frames whose kernel J lies in Fil A, is stable under φ₁ and on which φ₁ is topologically nilpotent, then α^* : Win(𝒜) → Win(𝒜′) is faithful.
hypotheses: Completeness is (p, ξ̃)-adic; topological nilpotence is pointwise.

For the topological faithfulness assertion the ambient rings and finite projective modules carry the separated complete adic topology of the cited prismatic frames, the frame maps and Frobenius are continuous, and the kernel topology is stated explicitly. An abstract radical-condition frame has no default topology.
proofSteps: φ₁(J) ⊆ J since B is ξ̃-torsion-free and φ(j) = ξ̃φ₁(j) (Anschütz–Le Bras, remark before the proof of Lemma 4.1.32, p. 37).
Essential surjectivity: normal decompositions exist over A_Nyg (node normal-decomposition with node henselian-projective-lifting) and the invertible Ψ lifts along the henselian surjection.

Full faithfulness: for β : M → JN define U(β) = φ_{N,1}^♯ ∘ (1 ⊗ β) ∘ (φ_{M,1}^♯)^{-1}; topological nilpotence of φ₁ on J makes Uⁿ(β) → 0, so a window map vanishing modulo J vanishes, and a module map that is a window map modulo J is corrected to a window map by the convergent series (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.1.32, pp. 37–39, following Lau 2010, Theorem 3.2).
Part (2) is the injectivity half of the same argument (Anschütz–Le Bras, Remark 4.1.34, p. 39).

Perform the successive correction on normal-decomposition coordinates using the partial inverse of the linearized window Frobenius on its specified image. Do not invert φ₁ : φ*Fil M → M on an arbitrary Nygaard filtration: that source need not be projective and the map need not be an isomorphism. The convergent correction is controlled by iterates of the divided Frobenius on the kernel (AL23 pp. 37–39).
acceptance: Applied in node PD.5/essential-surjectivity to Δ_S → B with S = Ā⟨X_j^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_j) and in node PD.7/breuil-kisin-comparison to the Breuil–Kisin prism.

The hypothesis cannot be dropped: for the kernel of A_crys(R) → W(R), R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x), the divided Frobenius fixes the nonzero element Σ_k p^k[x^{1/p^k}] (the 2025 erratum), so it is not topologically nilpotent there.

nodes.title: From the absolute prismatic topos to the quasi-syntomic topoi
nodes.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring, (R)_Δ its absolute prismatic site (bounded prisms (B, J) with a map R → B/J, flat topology), (R)_QSYN its big quasi-syntomic site (p-complete R-algebras with bounded p^∞-torsion, quasi-syntomic covers) and (R)_qsyn its small quasi-syntomic site. (1) The functor u : (R)_Δ → (R)_QSYN, (B, J) ↦ (R → B/J), is cocontinuous, hence defines a morphism of topoi u : Shv((R)_Δ) → Shv((R)_QSYN) whose inverse image u^{-1}F is the sheafification of ((B,J) ↦ F(B/J)) for sheaves F. (2) Restriction ε_* : Shv((R)_QSYN) → Shv((R)_qsyn) has a left adjoint ε^♮, which need not preserve finite limits. (3) Put v_* = ε_* ∘ u_* and v^♮ = u^{-1} ∘ ε^♮; then Rv_* ≅ Rε_* ∘ Ru_*.
hypotheses: R p-complete; all prisms bounded; set-theoretic cut-off as in PrismaticCohomology PR.1 (the results are independent of it).
Cocontinuity uses the lifting of quasi-syntomic covers to prisms (Bhatt–Scholze 7.11, PrismaticCohomology PR.2/quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms).

The big relative site (R)_QSYN has all p-complete R-algebras with bounded p∞-torsion as objects, with quasi-syntomic covers. Objects are not required to be absolutely quasi-syntomic over ℤ_p. The small site (R)_qsyn has quasi-syntomic R-algebras. The DD.5 absolute QSyn carrier alone does not identify these two sites.
proofSteps: A quasi-syntomic cover B/J → S lifts to a flat cover (B, J) → (C, JC) of prisms with S → C/JC (PrismaticCohomology PR.2/quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms); this is the cocontinuity condition (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 3.3.8 and Corollary 3.3.10, pp. 22–23; Stacks, Tag 00XJ).

Apply the cocontinuous-functor theorem for topoi to obtain sheafified restriction as inverse image (Stacks Tags 00XJ and 00XL). Mathlib CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCocontinuous records the covering-sieve condition; instantiate the separate adjunction and sheafification machinery rather than crediting the condition with constructing it.
ε_* is exact, which gives Rv_* = Rε_* ∘ Ru_* (Anschütz–Le Bras, §4.1, p. 27).

For an arbitrary sheaf F, inverse image is the sheaf associated to the presheaf (B,J) ↦ F(B/J), rather than that presheaf without sheafification; Stacks Tags 00XJ and 00XL supply the site-theoretic argument.

nodes.title: The quasi-syntomic sheaves O^pris, N^{≥1}O^pris and I^pris
nodes.statement: For a p-complete ring R put O^pris := v_*O_Δ, N^{≥1}O^pris := v_*N^{≥1}O_Δ and I^pris := v_*I_Δ on (R)_qsyn, where I_Δ ⊆ O_Δ is the ideal sheaf (B, J) ↦ J and N^{≥1}O_Δ = φ^{-1}(I_Δ) its first Nygaard piece. O^pris is a sheaf of δ-rings with Frobenius φ; I^pris is an invertible ideal of O^pris and N^{≥1}O^pris = φ^{-1}(I^pris). For R quasi-syntomic and R′ ∈ (R)_qsyn quasi-regular semiperfectoid, O^pris(R′) = Δ_{R′}, I^pris(R′) = IΔ_{R′} and N^{≥1}O^pris(R′) = N^{≥1}Δ_{R′}; thus O^pris is the sheaf Δ_• of PrismaticCohomology PR.7/quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison.

nodes.title: Prismatic Dieudonné crystals and admissibility
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic. A prismatic Dieudonné crystal over R is a finite locally free O^pris-module ℳ with a φ-semilinear map φ_ℳ : ℳ → ℳ whose linearisation φ^*ℳ → ℳ has cokernel killed by I^pris. Put Fil ℳ := φ_ℳ^{-1}(I^pris·ℳ). It is admissible if the image ℱ_ℳ of ℳ → ℳ → ℳ/I^pris·ℳ (first map φ_ℳ) is a finite locally free 𝒪-module and the induced map (O^pris/I^pris) ⊗_𝒪 ℱ_ℳ → ℳ/I^pris·ℳ is a monomorphism; here ℳ/I^pris·ℳ is an 𝒪 = O^pris/N^{≥1}O^pris-module through O^pris →φ O^pris → O^pris/I^pris. DM(R) is the category of prismatic Dieudonné crystals with O^pris-linear Frobenius-compatible maps and DM^adm(R) its full subcategory of admissible objects.
hypotheses: R quasi-syntomic; O^pris, I^pris, N^{≥1}O^pris of node opris-sheaves; 𝒪 ≅ O^pris/N^{≥1}O^pris by node opris-mod-nygaard.
proofSteps: Bundle (ℳ, φ_ℳ) with the cokernel condition (Anschütz–Le Bras, Definition 4.1.5, p. 28).

Linearised Frobenius: φ^*ℳ → ℳ is injective and becomes an isomorphism after inverting a local generator ξ̃ of I^pris, because its cokernel is ξ̃-torsion and φ^*ℳ is ξ̃-torsion-free (Remark 4.1.6, p. 29); so (ℳ, φ_ℳ) is a prismatic F-crystal in the sense of PrismaticCohomology PR.7 after node opris-vector-bundles.

Snake-lemma form of admissibility: with Q = coker(φ^*Fil ℳ → I^pris·ℳ) and K = coker(φ^*ℳ → ℳ), the snake lemma gives 0 → Q → (O^pris/I^pris) ⊗_𝒪 (ℳ/Fil ℳ) → ℳ/I^pris·ℳ → K → 0, so admissibility holds iff Q = 0 and ℳ/Fil ℳ is finite locally free (Remark 4.1.7, p. 29).

For Frobenius injectivity check equal source/target ranks locally using that Frobenius induces the identity on Spec(A/p); p is in the Jacobson radical. After inverting the prism ideal the map is an isomorphism, and I-torsion-freeness of a finite projective module gives injectivity before localization.
acceptance: The unit (O^pris, φ) is admissible with Fil = N^{≥1}O^pris and ℱ = 𝒪.
Admissibility is local on (R)_qsyn.

nodes.title: Prismatic Dieudonné modules over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-regular semiperfectoid with prism (Δ_R, I) (I principal) and θ : Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R ≅ R. A prismatic Dieudonné module over R is a finite projective Δ_R-module M with a φ-semilinear φ_M : M → M whose linearisation φ^*M → M has cokernel killed by I. It is admissible if the image F_M of M → M/IM (first φ_M) is a finite projective R-module and Δ_R/I ⊗_R F_M → M/IM is injective. DM(R) (resp. DM^adm(R)) is the category of (admissible) prismatic Dieudonné modules; the notation agrees with that for crystals through node crystals-modules-qrsp.
hypotheses: R quasi-regular semiperfectoid; R is a quotient of a perfectoid ring, so I = (ξ̃) is principal.
proofSteps: Bundle the data (Anschütz–Le Bras, Definitions 4.1.10 and 4.1.15, pp. 29, 31).
φ^*M → M is injective and an isomorphism after inverting ξ̃, and its cokernel is a finite projective Δ_R/I-module (Remark 4.1.11 with node PD.0/minuscule-cokernel-projective).
For R perfectoid, (Δ_R, I) = (A_inf(R), (ξ̃)) and DM(R) is the category of minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules (AInfCohomology AI.2/minuscule-prismatic-dictionary).
acceptance: The deliberate overloading of DM(R) for crystals and modules is justified by node crystals-modules-qrsp; statements such as Theorem 4.9.5 of the source speak of crystals where modules are meant (source issue E1).

nodes.title: Admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules are windows over the Nygaard frame
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-regular semiperfectoid and ξ̃ = φ(ξ) a generator of I, giving the Nygaard frame Δ_{R,Nyg} = (Δ_R, N^{≥1}Δ_R, φ, φ/ξ̃, ξ̃). (1) The forgetful functor Win(Δ_{R,Nyg}) → DM(R), (M, Fil M, φ_M, φ_{M,1}) ↦ (M, φ_M), is fully faithful with essential image DM^adm(R); its inverse sends (M, φ_M) to (M, φ_M^{-1}(IM), φ_M, φ_M/ξ̃). (2) For a quasi-syntomic map R → R′ of quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings and M′ = Δ_{R′} ⊗_{Δ_R} M, φ_{M′}^{-1}(IM′) = N^{≥1}Δ_{R′}·M′ + image of Δ_{R′} ⊗ φ_M^{-1}(IM).
hypotheses: R, R′ quasi-regular semiperfectoid; the Nygaard frame of node PD.0/prism-frames.
proofSteps: Δ_{R,Nyg} satisfies the hypotheses of node PD.0/window-filtration-frobenius-preimage: ξ̃ is a nonzerodivisor, N^{≥1}Δ_R = φ^{-1}(ξ̃Δ_R), and projectives lift along Δ_R → R because (Δ_R, N^{≥1}Δ_R) is henselian (node qrsp-prism-henselian).
Hence a window has Fil M = φ_M^{-1}(ξ̃M), which gives full faithfulness, and the image of φ_M modulo I is M/Fil M embedded as a direct summand: this is admissibility.

Conversely, for admissible (M, φ_M) the quadruple (M, φ_M^{-1}(IM), φ_M, φ_M/ξ̃) is a window; generation of M by φ_{M,1}(Fil M) follows from admissibility and the snake-lemma reformulation (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.1.29, p. 35).
Part (2) follows from (1) and base change of windows (node PD.0/window-base-change), whose filtration is generated by the image of Fil M and Fil Δ_{R′}·M′ (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.1.14, p. 30).
acceptance: For R = k a perfect field, a window over (W(k), pW(k), φ, φ/p) is a Dieudonné module with its Hodge filtration, and every prismatic Dieudonné module over k is admissible.

nodes.title: Over a perfectoid ring every prismatic Dieudonné module is admissible
nodes.statement: Let R be perfectoid, so (Δ_R, I) = (A_inf(R), (ξ̃)) with ξ̃ = φ(ξ) and N^{≥1}A_inf(R) = (ξ). Then DM^adm(R) = DM(R), and both equal the category of minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules over A_inf(R) with respect to ξ̃.
hypotheses: R perfectoid in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (integral perfectoid).
proofSteps: Since N^{≥1}A_inf(R) = (ξ), the Nygaard frame is the ξ-frame: Δ_{R,Nyg} = Δ_{R,ξ} (node PD.0/prism-frames).

By node nygaard-windows, DM^adm(R) ≃ Win(Δ_{R,ξ}); by the Cais–Lau equivalence (node PD.0/cais-lau-equivalence) Win(Δ_{R,ξ}) ≃ BK_min(A_inf(R)) for the ideal (ξ), i.e. DM(R′) for R′ = A_inf(R)/ξ; base change along the bijective φ identifies DM(R′) with DM(R).
The composite DM^adm(R) → DM(R) is the inclusion, so it is an equivalence (Anschütz–Le Bras, proof of Proposition 4.1.12, p. 36).
acceptance: For R = 𝒪_C, every minuscule BKF module (M, φ_M) has M/φ_M^{-1}(ξ̃M) finite free over 𝒪_C.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.1.12, p. 30, with proof on p. 36

nodes.title: Crystals and modules agree over a quasi-regular semiperfectoid ring
nodes.statement: For R quasi-regular semiperfectoid, evaluation on the initial prism, (ℳ, φ_ℳ) ↦ ((v^*ℳ)(Δ_R, I), v^*φ_ℳ), is an equivalence from prismatic Dieudonné crystals over R to prismatic Dieudonné modules over R, with quasi-inverse (M, φ_M) ↦ (M ⊗_{Δ_R} O^pris, φ_M ⊗ φ); it restricts to an equivalence between admissible crystals and admissible modules.
hypotheses: R quasi-regular semiperfectoid.
proofSteps: Without admissibility the equivalence is node opris-vector-bundles composed with evaluation at the final object of (R)_Δ.

Admissible modules give admissible crystals: by node nygaard-windows (2), for every quasi-regular semiperfectoid R′ over R the Hodge quotient of the base change is R′ ⊗_R (M/φ_M^{-1}(IM)), so ℳ/Fil ℳ ≅ 𝒪 ⊗_R (M/Fil M) is finite locally free.

Admissible crystals give admissible modules: the sequence 0 → Γ(Fil ℳ) → Γ(ℳ) → Γ(ℳ/Fil ℳ) is right exact by Nakayama after base change to perfect fields k, where every prismatic Dieudonné module is admissible (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.1.13 and its proof, pp. 30–31).
acceptance: For R perfectoid, a crystal is a minuscule BKF module tensored up to O^pris.

nodes.title: Filtered prismatic Dieudonné crystals
nodes.statement: A filtered prismatic Dieudonné crystal over a quasi-syntomic ring R is a triple (ℳ, Fil ℳ, φ_ℳ) with ℳ a finite locally free O^pris-module, Fil ℳ ⊆ ℳ an O^pris-submodule and φ_ℳ : ℳ → ℳ φ-semilinear such that (1) φ_ℳ(Fil ℳ) ⊆ I^pris·ℳ; (2) N^{≥1}O^pris·ℳ ⊆ Fil ℳ and ℳ/Fil ℳ is a finite locally free 𝒪-module; (3) φ_ℳ(Fil ℳ) generates I^pris·ℳ as an O^pris-module. DF(R) is their category. The forgetful functor DF(R) → DM(R) is fully faithful with essential image DM^adm(R), and its inverse sets Fil ℳ = φ_ℳ^{-1}(I^pris·ℳ).
hypotheses: R quasi-syntomic. This is the formulation of the earlier versions of the source; it is equivalent to admissibility.
proofSteps: Locally on (R)_qsyn reduce to R quasi-regular semiperfectoid and modules (node crystals-modules-qrsp).

There a filtered object is a window over the Nygaard frame with φ_{M,1} = φ_M/ξ̃: (1) is φ_M(Fil) ⊆ ξ̃M, (2) is the Hodge condition, (3) is the generation axiom; node nygaard-windows identifies windows with admissible modules and shows that Fil is forced to be φ_M^{-1}(IM) (Anschütz–Le Bras, Remark 1.3.3, p. 6; Lemma 4.1.23).
acceptance: The unit (O^pris, N^{≥1}O^pris, φ) is filtered.

The forgetful functor DF(R) → DM(R) is an equivalence when R is perfectoid or a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field (nodes admissible-over-perfectoid and PD.7/regular-automatic-admissibility).

nodes.title: A functorial resolution of an abelian group object of a topos
nodes.statement: Let G be an abelian group object of a topos 𝔛. There is a resolution C(G)_• = (… → ℤ[X₂] → ℤ[X₁] → ℤ[X₀]) → G, functorial in G, in which each X_i is a finite disjoint union of finite products of copies of G and ℤ[X] is the free abelian sheaf on X. Combined with node derived-yoneda, it computes RHom(G, F) by a spectral sequence with E₁-terms RΓ(G^{×n}, F).
hypotheses: 𝔛 a Grothendieck topos (here the prismatic or quasi-syntomic topos).
proofSteps: Construct it as in Breen's and Deligne's resolutions: the terms of the standard Mac Lane-type resolution of an abelian group are free abelian groups on finite products of the group, natural in the group, and the construction is compatible with sheafification (Anschütz–Le Bras, Theorem 4.4.1, p. 52, citing Scholze's lectures on condensed mathematics and Breen).
Use E₁^{a,b} = H^b(X_a,F); since X_a is already a finite coproduct, its cohomology includes the corresponding finite product of component cohomologies. No second unexplained direct sum is needed.
acceptance: For G = 0 every X_i is a point and the resolution computes Ext(0, F) = 0.

nodes.title: The prismatic Dieudonné functor
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic and G a p-divisible group over R, viewed as a sheaf on (R)_qsyn. The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of G is ℳ_Δ(G) := ℰxt¹_{(R)_qsyn}(G, O^pris), with φ_{ℳ_Δ(G)} induced by φ on O^pris. For R quasi-regular semiperfectoid, its prismatic Dieudonné module is M_Δ(G) := Ext¹_{(R)_qsyn}(G, O^pris) ≅ Ext¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ), with Frobenius induced by φ. Both are contravariant in G; ℳ_Δ is compatible with base change in R. Nodes PD.4/admissibility-and-lie and PD.4/pdiv-locally-free show that they land in DM^adm(R).
hypotheses: p-divisible groups are those of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4.5 (the carrier used by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1); they are syntomic sheaves on (R)_qsyn.
proofSteps: ℰxt¹ of abelian sheaves on the small quasi-syntomic site; φ acts through the coefficient sheaf (Anschütz–Le Bras, Definitions 4.2.1 and 4.2.8, pp. 39, 42).
Base change: ℰxt¹ commutes with restriction to slices (R)_qsyn/R′ ≅ (R′)_qsyn.
The module version is the value of ℳ_Δ(G) on R, since R is then final in its own small site and the Ext-sheaf is a crystal (node pushforward-description).

The cited supplier statements do not supply these specializations or derived compatibilities. PD.2 functor statements remain targets pending this infrastructure.

nodes.title: No homomorphisms from a p-divisible group to a derived p-complete sheaf
nodes.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group over a p-complete ring R. Then Hom(G, Q) = 0 for every derived p-complete abelian sheaf Q on (R)_QSYN or (R)_qsyn; in particular Hom(G, O^pris) = 0 and Hom(G, N^{≥1}O^pris) = 0.
hypotheses: G[p^n] finite locally free, hence syntomic; derived p-completeness of Q.
proofSteps: Multiplication by p is surjective on G in the syntomic topology, so the derived p-completion of G is T_pG[1]; maps from a complex in degrees ≤ −1 to one in degrees ≥ 0 vanish (Anschütz–Le Bras, Remark 4.2.2, p. 40).
acceptance: Hom(ℚ_p/ℤ_p, O^pris) = 0 since O^pris has no nonzero p-divisible elements.

sources.match: shows that p-divisible groups admit no nonzero maps to derived p-complete quasi-syntomic sheaves, because their derived p-completion is the Tate module in degree −1

nodes.title: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal as maps from the Tate module
nodes.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group over a quasi-syntomic ring R, with Tate module sheaf T_pG and universal cover G̃ = lim_{×p} G. (1) 0 → T_pG → G̃ → G → 0 is exact on (R)_qsyn, and its pullback by u^{-1} is exact on (R)_Δ. (2) ℳ_Δ(G) ≅ ℋom_{(R)_qsyn}(T_pG, O^pris) ≅ v_*ℋom_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}T_pG, O_Δ), compatibly with Frobenius.
hypotheses: T_pG and G̃ as in FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/universal-cover, restricted to the quasi-syntomic site.
proofSteps: (1): p is an epimorphism on G for the syntomic topology, so the limit sequence is exact (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.2.5, p. 41; R07.2.25 of the supplier for the fpqc version).

(2): apply RHom(−, O^pris) to (1); G̃ is uniquely p-divisible, so RHom(G̃, O^pris) = 0 since O^pris is derived p-complete; the connecting map gives ℋom(T_pG, O^pris) ≅ ℰxt¹(G, O^pris) (Lemma 4.2.6, p. 42).

The sequence 0 → T_pG → lim_[p]G → G → 0 on the quasi-syntomic site needs a compatible infinite p-root cover. Finite-level surjectivity of [p] and the fpqc universal-cover supplier alone do not prove this epimorphism on the specified site; use the recorded gap.

Closure gap — Compatible infinite p-root covers on the quasi-syntomic site: Plan a compatible tower of p-power-division covers of a p-divisible group whose completed limit is still a cover in the required quasi-syntomic site, and prove exactness of its inverse-limit sequence (AL23 Lemmas 4.2.5–4.2.6, pp. 41–43). Supply the analogous inverse-limit argument for truncated Ext crystals and étale Tate-module local triviality. R07.1/p-divisible-tate-module has a henselian local domain hypothesis and does not supply this sheaf statement.
acceptance: For G = ℚ_p/ℤ_p, T_pG = ℤ_p and ℳ_Δ = O^pris.
For G = μ_{p^∞}, T_pG = ℤ_p(1) and ℳ_Δ = ℋom(ℤ_p(1), O^pris) = O^pris{−1}.

sources.match: proves exactness of the universal cover sequence on the quasi-syntomic and prismatic sites and identifies the prismatic Dieudonné crystal with maps from the Tate module into O^pris

nodes.title: Hodge–Tate map and sequence of a p-divisible group
nodes.statement: For a p-divisible group G over 𝒪_C, with C algebraically closed and complete over ℚ_p, define α_G : T_pG → (Lie G*)∨ by Cartier duality and the invariant differential dlog on μ_{p∞}. The dual map, after the Tate twist, identifies Lie G ⊗ C(1) with the kernel in the functorial exact sequence 0 → Lie G⊗C(1) → T_pG⊗C → (Lie G*)∨⊗C → 0.
hypotheses: Lie modules are over 𝒪_C; the exact sequence is asserted after extension to C. C(1) = T_pμ_{p∞}⊗C.
proofSteps: A Tate vector in G pairs with G* into μ_{p∞}; differentiating this character gives α_G. Cartier duality gives the other map.

The Hodge–Tate exactness theorem is the key target, proved by the p-divisible-group Hodge–Tate comparison in SW20 Theorem 12.1.1, pp. 98–99; this is not merely dimension counting. The formal/rigid geometry input is included in the PD.3 period-theory gaps.
acceptance: The sequence has left dimension dim G and right dimension dim G*, summing to height G.

nodes.title: p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C are pairs (T, W) (Scholze–Weinstein Theorem B)
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed complete extension of ℚ_p. The functor G ↦ (T_pG, Lie G ⊗_{𝒪_C} C(1)) from p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C to pairs (T, W) of a finite free ℤ_p-module T and a C-subspace W ⊆ T ⊗_{ℤ_p} C is an equivalence of categories; W is embedded through the dual of the Hodge–Tate map α_{G^*} (Hodge–Tate sequence 0 → Lie G ⊗ C(1) → T_pG ⊗ C → (Lie G^*)^∨ ⊗ C → 0).
hypotheses: C algebraically closed and complete; Tate twist C(1) = T_pμ_{p^∞} ⊗ C.
In Example 12.1.6 use i = dim_projective(H)+1, equivalently the dimension of the rational vector-space hull of the line W; see independently checked source issue PrismaticCohomologyPartII/E5.
proofSteps: Use the Hodge–Tate map and sequence constructed in this roadmap (PD.3/p-divisible-hodge-tate-sequence), not an upward supplier.

Full faithfulness (Fargues): embed G into the multiplicative group G′ = T_pG(−1) ⊗ μ_{p^∞}; the generic fibre G^ad_η is the fibre product of G′^ad_η and Lie G ⊗ 𝔾_a over Lie G′ ⊗ 𝔾_a, so G^ad_η and then G = ⨆ Spf H⁰(Y, 𝒪⁺) are recovered from (T, W) (Scholze–Weinstein 2013, proof of Theorem 5.2.1, pp. 51–52).

Essential surjectivity for C spherically complete with surjective norm: define G^ad_η as that fibre product, show it is a p-divisible rigid-analytic group whose identity component is an open ball (Fargues, Corollaire 9 and Théorème 15; Scholze–Weinstein 2013, Proposition 5.2.5), and take G = ⨆ Spf H⁰(Y, 𝒪⁺) (pp. 52–53).

General C: realise (T, W) inside a Rapoport–Zink space using the description of the image of the period morphism (Scholze–Weinstein 2013, Theorem C, p. 6, and the proof of Theorem 5.2.1 for general C, p. 57).
acceptance: For dimension d = 1 and height h, W a line in C^h: G is isogenous to (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^{h−i} ⊕ G_i with G_i formal of height i, i = dim H + 1 for the smallest ℚ_p-rational projective subspace H containing W; W outside every rational hyperplane gives special fibre of height h (Drinfeld's Ω^h).

nodes.title: p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C are minuscule Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules
nodes.statement: Let C be algebraically closed complete over ℚ_p, A_inf = W(𝒪_C^♭), ξ a generator of ker θ. p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C are equivalent to finite free A_inf-modules M with a φ-linear isomorphism φ_M : M[1/ξ] ≅ M[1/φ(ξ)] such that M ⊆ φ_M(M) ⊆ φ(ξ)^{-1}M; equivalently, under Fargues' equivalence of BKF modules with pairs (T, Ξ) (T finite free over ℤ_p, Ξ a B_dR^+-lattice in T ⊗ B_dR), to the pairs with T ⊗ B_dR^+ ⊆ Ξ ⊆ ξ^{-1}T ⊗ B_dR^+.
hypotheses: Normalisation of the lectures (covariant, φ_M normalised by p^{-1} in characteristic p); node perfectoid-prismatic-classification relates it to the contravariant prismatic functor by the naive dual.
proofSteps: Lattices Ξ with T ⊗ B_dR^+ ⊆ Ξ ⊆ ξ^{-1}T ⊗ B_dR^+ correspond to C-subspaces W ⊆ T ⊗ C(−1) through Ξ/(T ⊗ B_dR^+) ⊆ ξ^{-1}T ⊗ B_dR^+/T ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ T ⊗ C(−1); the functor (T, W) ↦ (T, Ξ) is fully faithful (Scholze–Weinstein, Remark 12.4.7).

Compose Theorem B (node scholze-weinstein-theorem-b) with Fargues' classification of finite free BKF modules (AInfCohomology AI.2/fargues-classification); the lattice condition is the minuscule condition on M (Scholze–Weinstein, Theorem 14.1.1 and Theorem 14.4.1, pp. 115–121).
acceptance: In the covariant normalisation of the lectures, ℚ_p/ℤ_p ↦ (A_inf, φ) with φ_M(M) = M, and μ_{p^∞} ↦ (A_inf, φ(ξ)^{-1}φ) with φ_M(M) = φ(ξ)^{-1}M: the two extreme cases of the lattice condition.

After taking the naive dual and the Frobenius-shift dictionary ξ↔ξ̃, these are the effective minuscule modules of this roadmap PD.1/admissible-over-perfectoid. The AInf prismatic dictionary is not used circularly.

nodes.title: Every p-divisible group over 𝒪_C is a direct factor of that of a formal abelian variety
nodes.statement: For a p-divisible group G over 𝒪_C with Serre dual G^*, there is a formal abelian scheme 𝔄 over 𝒪_C with 𝔄[p^∞] ≅ G × G^*.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed complete over ℚ_p, residue field k.
proofSteps: The Newton polygon of G_k × G_k^* is symmetric, so there is an abelian variety A_k over k with A_k[p^∞] ≅ G_k × G_k^* (Oort).
p-divisible groups over 𝒪_C/p are isotrivial up to quasi-isogeny (Scholze–Weinstein 2013, Theorem 5.1.4(i)); changing A_k by a quasi-isogeny, lift it to A over 𝒪_C/p with A[p^∞] ≅ (G × G^*)_{𝒪_C/p}.
Serre–Tate: deforming A to 𝒪_C is equivalent to deforming its p-divisible group, giving 𝔄 (Scholze–Weinstein, Proposition 14.9.4, pp. 129–130).
acceptance: For G = μ_{p^∞}, G × G^* = μ_{p^∞} × ℚ_p/ℤ_p is the p-divisible group of an ordinary elliptic curve over 𝒪_C.

sources.locator: Appendix to Lecture 14, Proposition 14.9.4 and its proof, pp. 129–130
sources.match: proves that G × G^* is the p-divisible group of a formal abelian variety over 𝒪_C using Oort's existence theorem over the residue field, isotriviality over 𝒪_C/p and Serre–Tate deformation theory
every p-divisible group over 𝒪_C is isotrivial: its reduction to 𝒪_C/p is quasi-isogenous to a constant group

nodes.title: The crystalline Dieudonné module of G over 𝒪_C/p is M ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys
nodes.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group over 𝒪_C with Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module (M, φ_M) (node oc-minuscule-bkf). The p⁻¹-normalized covariant crystalline Dieudonné module of G_{𝒪_C/p} evaluated on A_crys(𝒪_C/p) is M ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys with φ_M ⊗ φ; hence the special fibre G_k corresponds under the same p⁻¹-normalized covariant classical Dieudonné theory to (M ⊗_{A_inf} W(k), φ_M ⊗ φ). There is a natural φ-equivariant isomorphism M_crys ⊗_{A_crys} B_crys ≅ T_pG ⊗_{ℤ_p} B_crys under which M_crys ⊗ B_dR^+ is the lattice Ξ (Faltings).
hypotheses: Covariant normalisation of the lectures; A_crys = A_crys(𝒪_C/p), the p-completed PD envelope of A_inf → 𝒪_C/p.

The Scholze–Weinstein covariant Frobenius is p⁻¹ times the usual covariant crystalline Frobenius. With this normalization the naive dual of the effective contravariant prismatic module matches M_SW; it is different from the Česnavičius–Scholze covariant convention in PD.6.
proofSteps: Faltings' comparison M_crys ⊗ B_crys ≅ T ⊗ B_crys with M_crys ⊗ B_dR^+ = Ξ (Scholze–Weinstein, Proposition 14.8.1), hence M_crys[1/p] ≅ M ⊗ B_crys^+ (Corollary 14.8.2).

Integrality M_crys ≅ M ⊗ A_crys (Proposition 14.8.3): reduce by node formal-abelian-variety-cover to G = 𝔄[p^∞] for a formal abelian variety, where both sides are the A_crys-cohomology H¹ and the comparison is the torsion-free A_crys comparison of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (AInfCohomology AI.4/absolute-crystalline-comparison), compatibly (Propositions 14.9.3–14.9.4, Corollary 14.9.2).
Base change A_crys → W(k) gives the special-fibre statement (Corollary 14.4.4).

CR.7/dieudonne-evaluation explicitly assumes characteristic p; that declaration alone does not provide this mixed-characteristic coefficient theory.

nodes.title: Dieudonné theory over integral perfectoid rings (Scholze–Weinstein, Lau)
nodes.statement: Let R be an integral perfectoid ring, ξ a generator of ker(θ : A_inf(R) → R). p-divisible groups over R are equivalent, functorially in R, to finite projective A_inf(R)-modules M with a φ-linear isomorphism φ_M : M[1/ξ] ≅ M[1/φ(ξ)] such that M ⊆ φ_M(M) ⊆ φ(ξ)^{-1}M. The equivalence M^SW is characterised by agreeing with (covariant, p^{-1}-normalised) Dieudonné theory when pR = 0 and with node oc-minuscule-bkf when R = 𝒪_C; and M ⊗_{A_inf(R)} A_crys^abs(R) is the Dieudonné module of G on the PD thickening A_crys^abs(R) → R, compatibly with φ_M.
hypotheses: Integral perfectoid in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (Scholze–Weinstein, Definition 17.5.1); PerfectoidQuotients Q0 integral algebra.
For p odd the theorem is also Lau 2018 (Theorem 9.8), through displays.

Here A_crys^abs(R) is the p-completed absolute PD envelope of A_inf(R) → R used in SW20 p. 158. In characteristic p it has extra divided powers of p and can have p-torsion; it maps to W(R) by giving p its usual divided powers. It is not the relative (ℤ_p,p)-PD envelope that equals W(R) for perfect R. Do not identify these two carriers using CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/fontaine-envelope.
Lau18 Theorem 9.8, p. 26, has p≥3. The all-p theorem here is SW20 Theorem 17.5.2; the two source scopes are not interchangeable.
proofSteps: pR = 0: Gabber's theorem (Lau 2013); the argument needs only perfect valuation rings, which is Berthelot's theorem (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2/berthelot-perfect-valuation-rings).
R = V a valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field of mixed characteristic: glue the 𝒪_K-case (node oc-minuscule-bkf) with the characteristic-p valuation ring V̄ along k, on both sides.

R = ∏ V_i a product of such valuation rings: categories of finite projective modules of fixed rank are products; compare with the crystalline module using the Faltings comparison of node bkf-crystalline-dieudonne factorwise and test integrality in each A_crys(V_i).

General R: both p-divisible groups over R and the module side satisfy v-descent along v-covers Spec S → Spec R^♭ (Bhatt–Scholze 2017), and R^♭ has a v-cover by a product of valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field (Scholze–Weinstein, proof of Theorem 17.5.2, pp. 158–160).

nodes.title: Hodge–Tate cohomology of an abelian scheme is an exterior algebra
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X the p-adic completion of an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over Ā = A/I. The conjugate spectral sequence E₂^{ij} = H^i(X, Ω^j_{X/Ā}){−j} ⇒ H^{i+j}(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) degenerates; every term and the abutment are finite locally free and commute with base change in (A, I); and H^*(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) ≅ Λ^* H¹(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) is the exterior Ā-algebra on H¹, of rank 2g.
hypotheses: (A, I) bounded; X proper smooth with the group structure of an abelian scheme.
proofSteps: Hodge cohomology of an abelian scheme is finite locally free, commutes with base change and is an exterior algebra on H¹ (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4/all-degree-exterior-cohomology, Berthelot–Breen–Messing 2.5.2).

The conjugate filtration of Hodge–Tate cohomology has graded pieces Ω^j{−j}[−j] (PrismaticCohomology PR.2/conjugate-filtration, PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison). The Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula-formal-schemes) and the Hopf-algebra structure from the group law force the cup product Λ^*H¹ → H^* to be an isomorphism by a rank count, hence degeneration (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.5.2, pp. 53–54).

Closure gap — Abelian lifting for the integral Hodge–Tate splitting at p=2: Give the unpolarized infinitesimal lifting of an abelian scheme needed to split τ≤1 of its Hodge–Tate complex over A/I (AL23 Proposition 3.2.1, Corollary 3.2.3 and the proof of Proposition 4.5.1, pp. 20–21, 53–54). The A4 Hodge/de Rham exterior theorem and its nilpotent-PD Grothendieck–Messing statement do not by themselves supply a lift along a general prism quotient A/I². This input is essential to the p=2 integral exterior-power argument.

For an elliptic curve, H¹(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) is locally free of rank 2 and H² ≅ Λ²H¹ of rank 1.

nodes.title: Primitive elements of an exterior algebra
nodes.statement: Let S be a commutative ring and M a projective S-module. The elements x of the exterior algebra Λ(M) with μ^*(x) = 1 ⊗ x + x ⊗ 1, where μ^* : Λ(M) → Λ(M ⊕ M) ≅ Λ(M) ⊗_S Λ(M) is induced by the diagonal M → M ⊕ M, are exactly Λ¹M = M.
hypotheses: M projective (finitely generated suffices for the use here).
proofSteps: Reduce to M free by a direct-summand argument; in degree n the component of μ^*(x) in Λ^a M ⊗ Λ^b M with a, b ≥ 1, a + b = n, is the (a, b)-shuffle coproduct of x, which is injective for n ≥ 2 when a = 1 (contracting with basis vectors), so primitives are concentrated in degree 1; degree 0 primitives satisfy x = 2x, so vanish (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.5.5, p. 56).
acceptance: M = S: Λ(S) = S ⊕ S·e, and the primitives are S·e.
Over S = F_2 and M = S², the element e₁ ∧ e₂ is not primitive.

nodes.title: Reduced prismatic Ext-sheaves of an abelian scheme
nodes.statement: Let R be p-complete and f : X → Spf R the p-adic completion of an abelian scheme of relative dimension g. Then ℰxt^i_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}X, Ō_Δ) = 0 for i = 0, 2, and ℰxt¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}X, Ō_Δ) is a prismatic crystal, isomorphic to R¹f_{Δ,*}Ō_Δ and locally free of rank 2g over Ō_Δ.
hypotheses: R p-complete; f_Δ : Shv((X)_Δ) → Shv((R)_Δ) the induced morphism of topoi.
proofSteps: Compute RHom(u^{-1}X, Ō_Δ) with the functorial resolution (node PD.2/functorial-resolution) and the derived Yoneda lemma (node PD.2/derived-yoneda): the E₁-terms are Hodge–Tate cohomologies of powers X^n, exterior algebras by node abelian-conjugate-degeneration and Künneth.
Ext⁰ and Ext² are cut out by primitive elements (node exterior-primitives) in degrees 0 and 2, which vanish; Ext¹ is the primitive part of H¹, i.e. all of H¹ = R¹f_{Δ,*}Ō_Δ.

Check the identification fibrewise at closed points: a map from a finitely generated module to a finite projective module that is an isomorphism on all fibres at closed points is an isomorphism (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.5.3 and Theorem 4.5.4, p. 55).

nodes.title: Prismatic Ext-sheaves of an abelian scheme
nodes.statement: With R, X, f as in node abelian-hodge-tate-ext: ℰxt^i_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}X, O_Δ) = 0 for i = 0, 2, and ℰxt¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}X, O_Δ) is a prismatic crystal isomorphic to R¹f_{Δ,*}O_Δ, locally free of rank 2g over O_Δ.

nodes.title: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of an abelian scheme
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic and X the p-completion of an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over R. Then ℳ_Δ(X[p^∞]) = ℰxt¹_{(R)_qsyn}(X[p^∞], O^pris) is a finite locally free O^pris-module of rank 2g, given by v_*R¹f_{Δ,*}O_Δ.

The exact sheaf sequence is 0 → X[p∞] → X → X[1/p] → 0. Tensoring with ℚ would also discard prime-to-p torsion and is not the stated sequence.

nodes.title: Prismatic cohomology of an abelian scheme
nodes.statement: With X as in node abelian-prismatic-ext, R^*f_{Δ,*}O_Δ is a finite locally free crystal on (R)_Δ and the exterior algebra on the locally free crystal R¹f_{Δ,*}O_Δ of rank 2g. In particular, for an abelian scheme over a bounded prism (A, I), each H^i_Δ(X/A) is finite locally free over A, and for the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)⟦u⟧, (E)) each full prismatic cohomology module H^i_Δ(X/A)/p is u-torsion-free over k⟦u⟧.

In the Breuil–Kisin example S = W(k)⟦u⟧, the u-torsion-free module is H^i_Δ(X/S)/p over S/p = k⟦u⟧. The reduced cohomology H^i(̄Δ)/p over 𝒪_K/p is killed by a power of u and does not satisfy that assertion.

Local freeness of all terms gives torsion-freeness of the reductions.

nodes.title: Prismatic Ext-sheaves of finite locally free group schemes
nodes.statement: Let R be p-complete and G a finite locally free commutative group scheme over R. Then ℰxt¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ) is a prismatic crystal of locally finitely presented O_Δ-modules.

The long exact sequence for 0 → G → X → X′ → 0 and node abelian-prismatic-ext present ℰxt¹(u^{-1}G, O_Δ) as the cokernel of a map of locally free crystals (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.6.2, p. 58).

nodes.title: Prismatic Ext-sheaves of truncated Barsotti–Tate groups
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic and G a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level n and height h over R. Then ℰxt¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ) is a prismatic crystal of finite locally free O_Δ/p^n-modules of rank h.

ℰxt¹(u^{-1}X′[p^n], O_Δ) = ℰxt¹(u^{-1}X′, O_Δ)/p^n is free of rank 2g over O_Δ/p^n; the sequence ℰxt¹(H) → ℰxt¹(X′[p^n]) → ℰxt¹(G) → 0 is right exact, and the outer terms are generated locally by 2g − h and h sections, so both are free of those ranks (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.6.4, pp. 59–61).

nodes.title: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group is locally free of rank the height
nodes.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group of height h over a quasi-syntomic ring R. Then ℰxt¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ) is a prismatic crystal of finite locally free O_Δ-modules of rank h, and ℰxt¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G, O_Δ)/p^n ≅ ℰxt¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}G[p^n], O_Δ). M → lim M/p^n is an isomorphism since Hom(u^{-1}G, O_Δ/p^n) = 0, which proves the crystal property (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.6.5, pp. 61–62).
The last sentence follows by node PD.1/opris-vector-bundles and node PD.2/pushforward-description.

nodes.title: O^pris and the crystalline structure sheaf in characteristic p
nodes.statement: For a quasi-syntomic F_p-algebra R′ there is a canonical isomorphism O^pris(R′) ≅ 𝒪^crys(R′) (the pushforward of the crystalline structure sheaf of the big crystalline site of R′ over ℤ_p, with Lau's p-th root topology) carrying N^{≥1}O^pris(R′) onto 𝒥^crys(R′), the pushforward of the PD ideal; it is compatible with Frobenius.

nodes.title: Comparison with the crystalline Dieudonné functor
nodes.statement: (1) Let R be quasi-syntomic with pR = 0 and G a p-divisible group over R. There is a canonical Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism ℳ_Δ(G) ≅ v^crys_*ℰxt¹_{(R/ℤ_p)_crys}((u^crys)^{-1}G, 𝒪_crys), linear over node opris-ocrys; for R quasi-regular semiperfect, M_Δ(G) ≅ 𝔻(G)(A_crys(R)). (2) Let R be quasi-syntomic and D → R a surjection from a p-complete p-torsion-free δ-ring whose kernel has divided powers, so that (D, (p)) ∈ (R)_Δ. For every p-divisible group G over R, v^*(ℳ_Δ(G))(D, (p)) ≅ 𝔻(G)(D), Frobenius-equivariantly, where 𝔻(G) is the contravariant crystalline Dieudonné crystal.

For the prismatic Dieudonné functor in part (2), R is quasi-syntomic. If D → R is the PD thickening, the crystalline-prism structure uses R → D/p induced by Frobenius on D (Frobenius kills the PD kernel modulo p); it is not a nonexistent reverse of the quotient D → R.

nodes.title: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group is admissible
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic and G a p-divisible group of height h over R with Cartier dual Ǧ. Choose a perfectoid S ↠ R, henselian along the kernel (Anschütz–Le Bras, Corollary 2.1.10); G lifts to a p-divisible group H over S (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/henselian-lifting-p-divisible), so ℳ_Δ(G) is the base change of ℳ_Δ(H), admissible by node PD.3/perfectoid-prismatic-classification; admissibility is stable under base change (Theorem 4.6.7, p. 63).

Lie(Ǧ): over the perfectoid S, the Hodge quotient of M_Δ(H) maps to the Hodge quotient of the crystalline Dieudonné module on A_crys(S) (node PD.3/scholze-weinstein-perfectoid, last clause), which is Lie(Ȟ) by the Hodge filtration of the crystalline Dieudonné crystal (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4.CR.7.2, CrystallineCohomology CR.7/messing-filtration-interface); base change to R (Anschütz–Le Bras, Remark 1.4.2, p. 7).

CR.7/dieudonne-evaluation explicitly assumes characteristic p; that declaration alone does not provide this mixed-characteristic coefficient theory.

Choose a perfectoid presentation S → R and p-complete the henselization of S along its kernel. PerfectoidQuotients Q0/completely-etale-and-henselian-perfectoid (AL23 Corollary 2.1.10, p. 14) supplies perfectoidness; the quotient remains R. This is the henselian presentation required for lifting G.

nodes.title: The q-logarithm and the divided q-logarithm
nodes.statement: (1) Let (B, J) be a prism over the q-de Rham prism (ℤ_p⟦q − 1⟧, ([p]_q)). For x ∈ 1 + N^{≥1}B of rank one (δ(x) = 0), log_q(x) = Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n−1} q^{−n(n−1)/2} (x − 1)(x − q)⋯(x − q^{n−1})/[n]_q converges in B, lies in N^{≥1}B, and equals ((q − 1)/log q)·log(x) in B[1/p]⟦x − 1⟧^∧_{(q−1)}. (2) If (B, J) is moreover bounded and x ∈ ℤ_p(1)(B/J) = T_p((B/J)^×), the Teichmüller-type lift [x^{1/p}]_θ̃ ∈ B has rank one and lies in 1 + N^{≥1}B, so ℓ_q(x) := log_q([x^{1/p}]_θ̃) ∈ B is defined; x ↦ ℓ_q(x) is a group homomorphism ℤ_p(1)(B/J) → B with φ(ℓ_q(x)) = [p]_q·ℓ_q(x).
hypotheses: [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1); [x^{1/p}]_θ̃ is the canonical rank-one lift of the compatible system of p-power roots through θ̃.
proofSteps: AL23 Lemma 2.2.2, p. 15 controls divisibility of the products by the q-integers and proves convergence in the prism topology; use that estimate, rather than claim denominators are harmless merely q-adically. The identity with the rescaled logarithm holds after rational formal completion.
For (2), rank-one elements with compatible p-power roots lie in 1 + N^{≥1}B by a δ-ring computation (Lemma 2.2.3, p. 15).
Frobenius: φ(log_q x) = ((q^p − 1)/log q^p)·log(x^p) = [p]_q log_q(x) by the comparison with log, which uses φ(q) = q^p and δ(x) = 0.
Compatibility with the prismatic logarithm of PrismaticCohomology PR.4/prismatic-logarithm: on the q-de Rham prism, ℓ_q and log_Δ differ by the generator e_A of A{1} with (q − 1)e_A = log_Δ(q^p).
acceptance: At q = 1 (after reduction to a crystalline prism) log_q becomes the classical logarithm log x = Σ (−1)^{n−1}(x − 1)^n/n.
ℓ_q(ε) for ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) is log_q(q^{1/p}·…) and is a generator of the twist after Proposition 4.7.3.

nodes.title: The prismatic Dieudonné crystal of an étale p-divisible group
nodes.statement: For R quasi-syntomic, ℳ_Δ(ℚ_p/ℤ_p) is the free O^pris-module generated by the class of the pushout of 0 → ℤ_p → ℚ_p → ℚ_p/ℤ_p → 0 along ℤ_p → O^pris, with Frobenius φ. More generally for G étale, ℳ_Δ(G) ≅ ℋom(T_pG, ℤ_p) ⊗_{ℤ_p} O^pris with Frobenius 1 ⊗ φ.
hypotheses: T_pG is a local system of finite free ℤ_p-modules on (R)_qsyn for G étale; ℤ_p denotes the sheaf of continuous ℤ_p-valued functions on π₀.
proofSteps: Node PD.2/tate-module-description: ℳ_Δ(G) = ℋom(T_pG, O^pris), and T_pG is locally ℤ_p^h (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.7.1, pp. 65–66).

Closure gap — Compatible infinite p-root covers on the quasi-syntomic site: Plan a compatible tower of p-power-division covers of a p-divisible group whose completed limit is still a cover in the required quasi-syntomic site, and prove exactness of its inverse-limit sequence (AL23 Lemmas 4.2.5–4.2.6, pp. 41–43). Supply the analogous inverse-limit argument for truncated Ext crystals and étale Tate-module local triviality. R07.1/p-divisible-tate-module has a henselian local domain hypothesis and does not supply this sheaf statement.

nodes.title: The Breuil–Kisin twist and ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞})
nodes.statement: Let O_Δ{−1} := ℋom_{(ℤ_p)_Δ}(u^{-1}ℤ_p(1), O_Δ) ≅ ℰxt¹(u^{-1}μ_{p^∞}, O_Δ), so that ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) ≅ v_*O_Δ{−1}. On the category of prisms over (ℤ_p⟦q − 1⟧, ([p]_q)), the O_Δ-linear map O_Δ → O_Δ{−1}, 1 ↦ ℓ_q, is an isomorphism, and φ(ℓ_q) = [p]_q·ℓ_q. Hence locally ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) ≅ (O^pris, ξ̃φ), and O_Δ{−1} is the inverse of the Breuil–Kisin twist O_Δ{1} of PrismaticCohomology PR.3.
hypotheses: The trivialisation is over prisms living over the q-de Rham prism; for general prisms O_Δ{−1} is invertible by descent.
proofSteps: For (B, J) over the q-de Rham prism, ℰxt¹(u^{-1}Ĝ_m|_{(B,J)}, O_Δ) is locally free of rank one and compatible with base change (node PD.4/pdiv-locally-free), so it suffices to prove surjectivity of 1 ↦ ℓ_q after base change to (W(k), (p)), k algebraically closed.

There the crystalline comparison (node PD.4/crystalline-comparison) reduces to the classical fact that the crystalline logarithm log[x] generates the crystalline Dieudonné crystal of μ_{p^∞} (Berthelot–Breen–Messing 2.2.3); at q = 1 the q-logarithm becomes log (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.7.3, pp. 66–67).
Frobenius: by node q-logarithm, φ(ℓ_q)(x) = [p]_q ℓ_q(x).

Agreement with O_Δ{1}^{-1}: both are invertible F-crystals on (ℤ_p)_Δ trivialised over the q-de Rham prism with Frobenius [p]_q, compatibly with the descent data (PrismaticCohomology PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples).

nodes.title: Compatibility with Cartier duality
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic and G a p-divisible group over R. The map Φ_G : ℳ_Δ(G)^∨ ⊗_{O^pris} ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) → ℳ_Δ(Ǧ), Φ_G(δ ⊗ l)(α) = (δ ∘ ℳ_Δ(α))(l) for α ∈ Hom(G, μ_{p^∞}) ≅ T_pǦ (using ℳ_Δ(Ǧ) ≅ ℋom(T_pǦ, O^pris)), is an isomorphism of prismatic Dieudonné crystals, where the source carries the Frobenius 1 ⊗ δ ⊗ l ↦ φ^*δ ∘ φ_{ℳ_Δ(G)}^{-1} ⊗ φ_{μ}(1 ⊗ l).
hypotheses: ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) is invertible (node bk-twist-trivialisation); ℳ_Δ(G)^∨ is the O^pris-linear dual.
proofSteps: Both sides are locally free of rank h (node PD.4/pdiv-locally-free), so it suffices to check surjectivity after base change to perfect fields k.

Over k, ℳ_Δ is the crystalline Dieudonné functor (node PD.4/crystalline-comparison); any natural transformation of this shape is determined by its value on μ_{p^∞}, so Φ_G = u·Φ^cl_G for the classical duality isomorphism Φ^cl and a unit u (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.6.9, pp. 64–65).

G = E[p^∞] for an elliptic curve: ℳ_Δ(G) is self-dual up to the twist ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞}), matching the Weil pairing.

nodes.title: The Tate module of the dual as Frobenius-fixed points
nodes.statement: For a quasi-regular semiperfectoid R with an orientation ξ̃, T_pG* is the kernel sheaf of φ/ξ̃−1 : N≥1ℳ_Δ(G) → ℳ_Δ(G). Moreover RΓ((R)_qsyn,T_pG*) is the derived fibre of φ/ξ̃−1 on the evaluated modules N≥1M_Δ(G) → M_Δ(G); the coefficient acyclicity on this basis justifies using evaluated modules rather than raw sheaves inside a global-sections formula.

Work locally over the cyclotomic q-de Rham prism so that ξ̃=[p]_q and the displayed divided-Frobenius normalization is the one in the source; the kernel descriptions glue independently of that choice.

(2) apply RHom(T_pG, −) and use T_pǦ = ℋom(T_pG, T_pG_m) and Ext¹(T_pG, T_pG_m) = Ext¹(G, μ_{p^∞}) = 0 locally (extensions of G by μ_{p^∞} split syntomic-locally since their splittings form a Ǧ-torsor) (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.8.2 and Remark 4.8.4, pp. 68–70).

Apply internal Rℋom(T_pG,−) to Bhatt–Lurie’s locally exact weight-one sequence, identify both coefficient Hom sheaves using PD.2, and only then apply RΓ. The weight-one supplier is a sheaf/local statement, not an exact sequence of global sections for arbitrary R. The dual group appears in the Tate module, while the two Dieudonné terms contain G (AL23 Remark 4.8.4, p. 70).

nodes.title: Full faithfulness over quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings
nodes.statement: For R quasi-regular semiperfectoid, M_Δ : BT(R) → DM(R) is fully faithful.
hypotheses: R quasi-regular semiperfectoid (reduce to R over ℤ_p^cycl by descent).
Full faithfulness means Hom(G,H) ≃ Hom_DM(ℳ_Δ(H),ℳ_Δ(G)); the direction of the two inputs is reversed.
proofSteps: Write ℛ : Sh_R^op → 𝒟_R, F ↦ ℋom(F, O^pris), from abelian sheaves to O^pris[F]-modules, with left adjoint ℒ(M) = ℋom_{O^pris[F]}(M, O^pris); M_Δ(G) = ℛ(T_pG) (node PD.2/tate-module-description).

For F = T_pG the counit ℒℛF → F is an isomorphism: node tate-module-recovery applied to Ǧ gives F ≅ (ℳ_Δ(Ǧ))^{φ = ξ̃}, and Cartier duality (node cartier-duality) with ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) = (O^pris, ξ̃φ) rewrites this as ℒ(ℳ_Δ(G)).

The two natural isomorphisms differ by a natural endomorphism of all p-divisible groups, i.e. a locally constant scalar in ℤ_p; it is a unit, as seen on ℚ_p/ℤ_p (Anschütz–Le Bras, Theorem 4.8.1 and Proposition 4.8.3, pp. 68–70).

nodes.title: Essential surjectivity over quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings
nodes.statement: For R quasi-regular semiperfectoid, M_Δ : BT(R) → DM^adm(R) (admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules) is essentially surjective.
hypotheses: The source states the target as admissible crystals; modules are meant (source issue AL23 E1 of the paper extraction, recorded in sourceIssues).
proofSteps: It suffices to work on a quasi-syntomic cover: descent data for M_Δ(G′) give descent data for G′ by full faithfulness (node full-faithfulness) and p-divisible groups form a stack (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/p-complete-flat-descent).

Choose a perfect prism (A, I) with Ā = A/I ↠ R, henselian along the kernel, and (after a cover) generators a_j of the kernel with compatible p-power roots; put S = (Ā⟨X_j^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_j))^∧ and S̃ = Ā⟦X_j^{1/p^∞}⟧ (perfectoid).

DM^adm(S) → DM^adm(R) is essentially surjective: Δ_S → Δ_R is surjective by the Hodge–Tate comparison and henselian along its kernel; lift windows by normal decompositions (Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.9.1).

DM^adm(S̃) → DM^adm(S) is essentially surjective: Δ_S = Δ_S̃{X_j/ξ̃}^∧, the kernel K of α : Δ_S → B = Δ_S̃/(X_j) is topologically generated by z_{j,n} = X_j^{p^n}/(φ^n(ξ̃)⋯ξ̃^{p^n}) (PrismaticCohomology PR.0/prismatic-envelope-rank-one-presentation), φ(K) ⊆ ξ̃Δ_S and φ/ξ̃ is topologically nilpotent on K (Lemma 4.9.3), so windows over Δ_S and B agree (node PD.0/window-deformation); windows over B lift to Δ_S̃ by henselian lifting of unit φ-modules (node PD.0/unit-frobenius-deformation) (Lemmas 4.9.2–4.9.4).
Over the perfectoid S̃ every admissible module comes from a p-divisible group (node PD.3/perfectoid-prismatic-classification); base change to R (Theorem 4.9.5, pp. 73–74).

nodes.title: Prismatic Dieudonné theory classifies p-divisible groups (Anschütz–Le Bras)
nodes.statement: Let R be a quasi-syntomic ring. The prismatic Dieudonné functor ℳ_Δ : BT(R) → DM^adm(R), G ↦ (ℳ_Δ(G), φ_{ℳ_Δ(G)}), is an antiequivalence between p-divisible groups over R and admissible prismatic Dieudonné crystals over R. It is exact, compatible with base change in R and with Cartier duality (node cartier-duality), ℳ_Δ(G) has rank the height of G and ℳ_Δ(G)/Fil ≅ Lie(Ǧ) ⊗ 𝒪. The same holds for p-divisible groups over a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme.
hypotheses: R quasi-syntomic (p-complete, bounded p^∞-torsion, L_{R/ℤ_p} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]).
proofSteps: Both sides are stacks for the quasi-syntomic topology (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/p-complete-flat-descent; node PD.1/dieudonne-crystal-stack), and quasi-regular semiperfectoid rings form a basis (DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.5/qrsp-refinement), so assume R quasi-regular semiperfectoid.

There crystals are modules (node PD.1/crystals-modules-qrsp), the functor lands in admissible objects (node PD.4/admissibility-and-lie), and it is fully faithful (node full-faithfulness) and essentially surjective (node essential-surjectivity) (Anschütz–Le Bras, Theorem 4.6.10, p. 65; Theorems 1.4.1 and 1.4.4 of the introduction, pp. 7–8).
Formal schemes: glue over an affine open cover using the stack property.

R = k perfect: classical Dieudonné modules (node PD.4/classical-comparison).
R = 𝒪_K: minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules (node PD.7/breuil-kisin-comparison).
R = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ (p-adically completed polynomial ring, quasi-syntomic and not quasi-regular semiperfectoid): p-divisible groups are admissible crystals glued from a perfectoid cover.

nodes.title: An explicit quasi-inverse, and étale p-divisible groups as unit-root crystals

nodes.title: Torsion prismatic Dieudonné modules over a perfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let R be perfectoid, ξ a generator of ker θ and ξ̃ = φ(ξ). A torsion prismatic Dieudonné module over R is a triple (M, φ_M, ψ_M) with M a finitely presented A_inf(R)-module of projective dimension ≤ 1 killed by a power of p, φ_M : M → M φ-semilinear and ψ_M : M → M φ^{-1}-semilinear, such that φ_M ∘ ψ_M = ξ̃ and ψ_M ∘ φ_M = ξ. DM_tors(R) is the exact category of these, with maps commuting with φ_M and ψ_M and exact sequences those of underlying modules.
hypotheses: R perfectoid. The two relations use the semilinearity conventions of the source: φ_M ∘ ψ_M is multiplication by ξ̃ and ψ_M ∘ φ_M multiplication by ξ.
proofSteps: Bundle the data (Anschütz–Le Bras, Definition 5.1.1, p. 75).

Locally on Spec R every object is the cokernel of an injective map of prismatic Dieudonné modules (an isogeny), because a finitely presented p-power-torsion module of projective dimension ≤ 1 has a two-term resolution by finite projectives on which φ_M lifts (Lau 2018, Lemma 10.10).
acceptance: For pⁿ : M → M, the quotient has induced semilinear maps φ_M and ψ_M satisfying φ_Mψ_M=ξ̃ and ψ_Mφ_M=ξ. The inverse-type map is the one from the integral Frobenius matrix factorization; a rational inverse is not automatically an endomorphism of a torsion module.

nodes.title: Classification of finite locally free group schemes over a perfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let R be perfectoid. There is a natural exact antiequivalence H ↦ (M_Δ(H), φ_{M_Δ(H)}, ψ_{M_Δ(H)}) from the exact category of finite locally free commutative group schemes of p-power order over R to DM_tors(R), with M_Δ(H) = Ext¹_{(R)_Δ}(u^{-1}H, O_Δ) and φ induced by the Frobenius of O_Δ; its quasi-inverse is exact as well.
hypotheses: R perfectoid; no restriction on p (Lau 2018, Theorem 10.12 needs p ≥ 3).
All primes are included by AL23 Theorem 5.1.4; Lau18 Theorem 10.12 alone is stated for p≥3 and is not an all-p supplier.
proofSteps: Construction: Zariski-locally every H is the kernel of an isogeny of p-divisible groups of abelian schemes (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/raynaud-abelian-embedding), and every torsion module the cokernel of an isogeny of prismatic Dieudonné modules; apply node PD.3/perfectoid-prismatic-classification in place of Lau's Theorem 9.8 (Anschütz–Le Bras, proof of Theorem 5.1.4, p. 76).
M_Δ(H) = Ext¹(u^{-1}H, O_Δ): for H = ker(X → X′), Ext¹(u^{-1}X, O_Δ) → Ext¹(u^{-1}H, O_Δ) is surjective because Ext²(u^{-1}X′, O_Δ) = 0 (node PD.4/abelian-prismatic-ext).

Exactness: surjectivity of M_Δ(H) → M_Δ(H′) is local and reduces to abelian schemes as above; injectivity of M_Δ(H″) → M_Δ(H) needs Hom(u^{-1}H′, O_Δ) = 0, which holds as it is p-power torsion and embeds in H⁰(H′, Δ_{H′/A_inf}), p-torsion-free for the p-completely syntomic H′ (PrismaticCohomology PR.1/p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic).
Exactness of the inverse: by node torsion-base-change and compatibility with base change reduce to R a perfect field (Gabber–Ramero), where both categories are abelian (Anschütz–Le Bras, p. 77).

nodes.title: Cartier duality for finite locally free group schemes
nodes.statement: Let R be perfectoid, A=A_inf(R), H a finite locally free group scheme of p-power order, and L=M_Δ(μ_{p∞}). There is a natural identification of underlying A-modules M_Δ(H*) ≃ Ext¹_A(M_Δ(H),A)⊗_A L. Its Frobenius and inverse-type operator are induced by dualizing an isogeny presentation; this gives Cartier duality in the torsion category. The twist L is indispensable.
hypotheses: M_Δ(H) is finitely presented of projective dimension at most one and killed by a p-power. The formula is asserted on perfectoid bases only.
proofSteps: Locally write H=ker(G₀→G₁) with a p-isogeny of p-divisible groups. Contravariance gives 0→M₁→M₀→M_Δ(H)→0.
Cartier duality of p-divisible groups identifies M_Δ(Gᵢ*) with Mᵢ∨⊗L. The cokernel of M₀∨⊗L→M₁∨⊗L is Ext¹_A(M_Δ(H),A)⊗L; Hom_A(M_Δ(H),A)=0 since A is p-torsion-free.

Transport the two operators through these dual presentations. Independence of the presentation and gluing follow from the finite-group classification and the functorial duality of p-divisible groups. This is a deduction from the two cited results, not the content of Remark 5.1.7.
acceptance: Over a perfect field k, Cartier duality exchanges ℤ/p and μ_p. Omitting L would leave the Frobenius twist wrong.
The zero group gives the zero module, and applying Cartier duality twice gives back H.

nodes.title: The covariant prismatic Dieudonné module over perfectoid rings
nodes.statement: Let A be perfectoid and ξ a generator of ker(A_inf(A) → A). The functor G ↦ 𝕄(G) := Ext¹_{A_Δ}(u^{-1}G^*, 𝒪_Δ) = M_Δ(G^*) is a covariant equivalence, compatible with base change, from commutative finite locally free A-groups of p-power order to finitely presented p-power-torsion A_inf(A)-modules of projective dimension ≤ 1 with a Frob-semilinear F and a Frob^{-1}-semilinear V such that FV = Frob(ξ) and VF = ξ; it is exact with exact inverse, 𝕄(μ_{p^n}) = (A_inf/p^n, F = Frob, V = ξ·Frob^{-1}), 𝕄(ℤ/p^n) = (A_inf/p^n, F = Frob(ξ)·Frob, V = Frob^{-1}), and for the p^n-torsion of a p-divisible group 𝕄(G) is finite projective over A_inf/p^n. For perfect F_p-algebras it agrees with the crystalline functor of node perfect-base-classification.
hypotheses: Česnavičius–Scholze write ξ for the generator called ξ here and Frob(ξ) for ξ̃; the passage G ↦ G^* converts the contravariant functor of node finite-group-classification into a covariant one, exchanging the roles of φ and ψ.

Constant height determines a constant rank; it does not trivialize a vector bundle over a nonlocal ring. In the covariant convention evaluate the contravariant functor on G* and retain its φ and ψ; Cartier duality is not defined by simply swapping the two semilinear operators on the same module.
proofSteps: Compose node finite-group-classification with Cartier duality (exact) and set F = φ_{M_Δ(G^*)}, V = ψ_{M_Δ(G^*)} (Česnavičius–Scholze, §4.2.1, p. 41).
Examples: Anschütz–Le Bras, Lemma 4.7.1 for ℤ/p^n and node PD.5/bk-twist-trivialisation for μ_{p^n} (Česnavičius–Scholze, Example 4.2.2).
Exactness: Lemma 4.2.3 of Česnavičius–Scholze, from the exactness in node finite-group-classification.

nodes.title: Crystalline Dieudonné theory over perfect F_p-schemes (Berthelot, Gabber, Lau)
nodes.statement: For a perfect F_p-scheme S there is a covariant equivalence G ↦ 𝕄(G) from commutative finite locally free S-groups locally of p-power order to quasi-coherent W(𝒪_S)-modules 𝕄 with Frobenius-semilinear F and Frobenius^{-1}-semilinear V, FV = VF = p, whose sections over every affine Spec R ⊆ S are finitely presented over W(R), killed by a power of p and of projective dimension ≤ 1. Zariski-locally 𝕄(G) = coker(𝕄(H₀) ↪ 𝕄(H₁)) for 0 → G → H₀ → H₁ → 0 with H_i p-divisible, where 𝕄(H) is the value of the covariant Dieudonné crystal ℰxt¹_crys(H^*, 𝒪) on (S, W_n(𝒪_S))_n; its formation commutes with base change along perfect S-schemes; it is exact with exact inverse; 𝕄(ℤ/p^n) = (W(𝒪_S)/p^n, F = p·Frob, V = Frob^{-1}) and 𝕄(μ_{p^n}) = (W(𝒪_S)/p^n, F = Frob, V = p·Frob^{-1}). On affine perfect S = Spec R it agrees with node covariant-normalisation for the perfectoid ring R (ξ = p).
hypotheses: S perfect of characteristic p; W(𝒪_S) the Zariski sheaf of Witt vectors.
proofSteps: Affine case S = Spec R: R is perfectoid with A_inf(R) = W(R) and ξ = p; node covariant-normalisation gives the equivalence, and node PD.4/crystalline-comparison identifies 𝕄 with the crystalline covariant module (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.3.6 for perfect R; Česnavičius–Scholze, §4.1.1 and §4.2.1, pp. 36, 41).
Glue Zariski-locally: both sides are Zariski sheaves and the functor commutes with localisation and perfect base change.

Exactness: the crystalline Dieudonné functor on p-divisible groups is exact (Berthelot–Breen–Messing 1.1.7, 3.3.3), and the snake lemma after embedding short exact sequences into sequences of p-divisible groups (Česnavičius–Scholze, Lemma 4.1.3, p. 36).

The theorem was first Gabber's (unpublished, after Berthelot 1980, Théorème 3.4.1 for perfect valuation rings, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2/berthelot-perfect-valuation-rings) and was reproved by Lau (2013, Corollary 6.5).

nodes.statement: Let R be a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field k of characteristic p. There is a quasi-syntomic cover R → R_∞ with R_∞ perfectoid.

nodes.title: p-divisible groups over 𝒪_K are minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules (prismatic proof)
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete regular local ring of dimension at most one with perfect residue field k of characteristic p. For dimension zero use (A,I)=(W(k),(p)); for R=k⟦u⟧ use (W(k)⟦u⟧,(p)); for a mixed-characteristic DVR use its Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)⟦u⟧,(E(u))), with δ(u)=0. The target is the contravariant equivalence BT(R)^op ≃ BK_min(A) given by evaluating the prismatic Dieudonné crystal. The mixed-characteristic case recovers Kisin for odd p and Kim–Lau–Liu for p=2; the characteristic-p connection step remains a recorded gap.
hypotheses: dim R ≤ 1, i.e. R = 𝒪_K for a complete discretely valued K of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field, R = k⟦u⟧, or R = k. The source states the theorem for every complete regular local ring but writes its proof only for d = 1 (source issue PrismaticCohomologyPartII/E1); for d ≥ 2 the classification of p-divisible groups by Breuil windows over W(k)⟦u₁, …, u_d⟧ is Lau's (p odd, Lau 2010, Theorem 1.1; p = 2, Lau 2014), whose identification with the prismatic functor is a recorded gap.

For dim R=0, R=k and use (A,I)=(W(k),(p)). For dim R=1 in characteristic p, use (W(k)⟦u⟧,(p)); p is not an Eisenstein polynomial in u. The mixed-characteristic DVR case uses its actual Eisenstein polynomial E(u).

R p-torsion-free: by node PD.5/main-classification and node regular-automatic-admissibility, BT(R)^op ≃ DM(R). The Breuil–Kisin prism covers the final object of Shv((R)_Δ) (Lemma 5.2.7: any prism lifts R → R_∞ by Proposition 3.3.8, and then lives over the perfection of A), so a crystal is a minuscule Breuil–Kisin module over A with a descent datum over the self-coproduct B = A ⊗̂ A.

The descent datum is automatic: for the kernel J of B → A, J ⊆ N^{≥1}B, φ₁(J) ⊆ J and φ₁ = φ/E is topologically nilpotent on J (Lemma 5.2.8), so window base change along B → A is fully faithful (node PD.0/window-deformation) and evaluation on (A, I) is an equivalence (Anschütz–Le Bras, Theorem 5.2.5 and Lemmas 5.2.7–5.2.8, pp. 79–85).

Closure gap — Characteristic-p connection in the regular Breuil–Kisin comparison: For R=k⟦u⟧ prove existence and uniqueness of the integrable topologically quasi-nilpotent horizontal connection on the relevant minuscule module, as used in AL23 Theorem 5.2.5, p. 79 (which refers to de Jong Proposition 2.7.3). The general crystalline evaluation supplier does not state this automatic-connection theorem. The mixed-characteristic DVR proof in AL23 pp. 79–84 does not prove this separate characteristic-p step.

nodes.title: The Witt frame
nodes.statement: For a ring R in which p is nilpotent, or a p-adically complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion, the Witt frame is 𝒲_R = (W(R), I_R = V(W(R)) = ker(W(R) → R), F, F₁ = V^{-1}, p): F is the Witt Frobenius and F₁ : I_R → W(R) the inverse of the injective Verschiebung onto I_R, so F = p·F₁ on I_R. It is a frame in Lau's sense (I_R + pW(R) lies in the radical of W(R)); its formation is functorial in R and defines a frame of sheaves W(𝒪) on the p-completely faithfully flat site of R.
hypotheses: Frames in Lau's generality (node PD.0/frame with completeness replaced by I_R + pW(R) ⊆ Rad W(R)).
proofSteps: V is injective with image I_R; F(V(x)) = p·x gives F = pF₁ on I_R (Mathlib WittVector.frobenius and WittVector.verschiebung, with WittVector.frobenius_verschiebung).
I_R + pW(R) lies in the radical since R is p-adically complete (Zink 2002, §1; Lau 2010, §2, the Witt frame example).
acceptance: For k perfect, 𝒲_k = (W(k), pW(k), F, F/p, p).
For R = F_p[ε]/ε², I_R contains V([ε]) with F₁(V[ε]) = [ε].
