nodes.title: Displays
nodes.statement: For p-complete R with bounded p∞-torsion, a display in the convention of this roadmap is a window (P,Q,F,F₁) over the Witt frame 𝒲_R, equivalently a window over W(𝒪) on the p-completely faithfully flat site. P is finite projective over W(R), I_RP⊆Q⊆P, P/Q is finite projective over R, and F and F₁ obey the window semilinearity, relation and generation axioms. Here F₁ on Q is part of the module data; only the coefficient frame map on I_R is V⁻¹. F-nilpotence means local nilpotence of F modulo p. These all-window objects are Zink’s 3n-displays (Definition 1); his Definition 2 reserves “display” for the V-nilpotent subclass.
hypotheses: p-complete R with bounded p^∞-torsion for the descent statement.
proofSteps: Window over 𝒲 (node witt-frame, node PD.0/window).

Displays satisfy faithfully flat descent (Zink 2002, Theorem 37), and over p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion are compatible systems of displays over R/p^n, so the sheaf-theoretic definition agrees with windows over 𝒲_R (Anschütz–Le Bras, Definition 5.3.1 and Remark 5.3.2, pp. 87–88).

The distinguished-element condition makes v a unit. For p-torsion-free R the divided equation follows after multiplying by p; in characteristic p use the divided-Frobenius compatibility argument cited in AL23 Proposition 5.3.3, p. 88. The scalar written there with p=u f(ξ̃) is v⁻¹ and is inconsistent with its earlier u-morphism convention (source issue E3).

nodes.title: The display of a p-divisible group
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic. For G ∈ BT(R) put Z_R(G) = ℳ_Δ(G) ⊗_{O^pris} W(𝒪) with Frobenius φ ⊗ F, and Fil Z_R(G) generated by I(𝒪)·Z_R(G) and the image of φ^{-1}(I^pris·ℳ_Δ(G)). There is a unique way to complete this to a functor Z_R : BT(R)^op → Disp(R), natural in R, which for R quasi-regular semiperfectoid with pR = 0 or R p-torsion-free is the composite of ℳ_Δ (as windows over the Nygaard frame, node PD.1/nygaard-windows) with base change along the frame map of node nygaard-to-witt-frame. For p = 2 the functor is not an antiequivalence on all p-divisible groups.
hypotheses: R quasi-syntomic.
proofSteps: For the QRSP characteristic-p or p-torsion-free cases, base change the Nygaard window along the correctly normalized v-morphism; this gives a contravariant display functor.

To extend to general quasi-syntomic R in the stated flatness range, the proposed universal construction requires a p-torsion-free smooth presentation of the moduli of full p-divisible groups, together with its relation space and compatibility of the universal windows. Descent of displays then defines Z_R and its naturality. R07.2/bt-stack-smooth states smoothness only for BT_n, not this compatible full-BT presentation; see the recorded gap.

Prove p-torsion-freeness of the completed presentation rings and that the universal Nygaard-window construction descends naturally along the relation. Smoothness at each finite level does not by itself prove this assertion (AL23 Proposition 5.3.4, pp. 88–89).

nodes.title: Formal p-divisible groups over general bases
nodes.statement: Over a ring on which p is nilpotent, a formal p-divisible group is a commutative formally smooth finite-dimensional formal Lie group, locally given on nilpotent R-algebras by a power-series formal group law, for which [p] is finite locally free and the associated p-power-torsion fppf sheaf is a Barsotti–Tate group. Over a p-complete ring use compatible such objects over R/pⁿ, with the corresponding compatible Barsotti–Tate group. Write BT_f(R) for this category.
hypotheses: No noetherian or local hypothesis on R. Dimension is locally constant. This is a formal Lie group on nilpotent test algebras, not an assertion that every section of its associated torsion sheaf over every algebra is nilpotent.
proofSteps: Use formal power-series laws Zariski-locally, with coordinate-free gluing on nilpotent algebras; impose formal smoothness and finite locally free p-multiplication. The BT sheaf and compatible p-adic systems are part of the definition. Zink’s introductory Nil_R framework supplies the needed general-base carrier.
acceptance: On complete noetherian local rings this agrees with the formal Lie carrier of R07.1; that agreement does not extend the hypotheses of the R07 declaration itself.

For n≥1, α_*(ℤ/pⁿ)≃(O^pris/pⁿ)^{φ=1} and (α∘j)_*(ℤ/pⁿ)≃((O^pris/pⁿ)[1/I])^{φ=1}. For a p-divisible G, j*α*(((ℳ_Δ(G)/pⁿ)[1/I])^{φ=1})≃Hom_{ℤ/pⁿ}(G[pⁿ]_η,ℤ/pⁿ), and (α∘j)*G[pⁿ]≃G[pⁿ]_η. Fixed points here are non-derived.

restructure.detail: The design job combined six paper routes into one Part II of PrismaticCohomology. They form four independent directions with disjoint final theorems: (A) prismatic Dieudonné theory (Anschütz–Le Bras; Česnavičius–Scholze §4; Scholze–Weinstein Lectures 12, 14, 17), whose endpoint is the classification of p-divisible groups over quasi-syntomic rings; (B) prismatic F-crystals and crystalline local systems on smooth formal schemes (Guo–Reinecke, 167 items), whose endpoint is the relative C_crys conjecture with coefficients; (C) F-smoothness and p-adic étale Tate twists (Bhatt–Mathew, 60 items), whose endpoint is the identification of syntomic complexes of F-smooth schemes with étale Tate twists and Sato's complexes; (D) the integral Riemann–Hilbert functor and Cohen–Macaulay vanishing (Bhatt et al., 5 items). None of B, C, D uses the Dieudonné classification beyond a unit test (Guo–Reinecke mention the Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group as an example), and A uses none of them. Combined they would far exceed one roadmap and obscure ownership. As the job instructions permit, this packet plans direction A, the first direction listed, as PrismaticCohomologyPartII.
